title: POST /api/documents/:id/anchor has no role, owner or revoked-document check: any authenticated tenant user can trigger a re-anchor
description:
**BLUF:** Surface: originate `POST /api/documents/:id/anchor`, the retry route. I read the route and every layer in front of and behind it at develop `6d41673e0f79`. The only gates are authentication (a Bearer token and an active session), tenant scoping, and the refusal "Document is already anchored". There is no role gate, no owner check and no terminal-status guard. So any authenticated user in the tenant, including the public-signup `OWNER` role, which the share and transfer-custody gates exclude by design (`middleware/documentWriteRoles.ts:24-27`), can make originate call the anchoring service for a document whose blob is missing or `anchor_failed`; on success the route writes `status: 'anchored'` over the document, revoked or deleted ones included. This is a source reading. I ran no request against any box and did not execute the route.

**Route** (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`, `:1437-1571`):

* `:1442` `getUserFromRequest` and a 401 when absent; `:1449` `getDocument(id, tenantId, req.db)` and a 404 when the document is not found in the caller's tenant.
* `:1458` the only state check: `if (document.blockchain && document.blockchain.status !== 'anchor_failed')` then 400 "Document is already anchored". A document with no blob at all passes it.
* `:1474-1478` it calls `${ANCHORING_SERVICE_URL}/api/anchors` with the caller's own `Authorization` header; `:1489` the body carries `...anchorIdentityFields(req.body)`, so the caller's request body supplies the identity fields (the comment above it, `:1488`, is "the re-anchor path carries S's identity too").
* `:1534-1537` `updateDocument(id, tenantId, { blockchain, status: 'anchored' })` with no options; `:1545` starts the confirmation poll; `:1560` answers 202.
* Within `:1437-1571` there is none of `ALLOWED_*_ROLES`, `DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES`, `hasAnyRole`, `requireRole`, `requireSelfOrRole` or `requireScope` (census of the file below).

**Siblings in the same file:** `POST /` (`:373`, `ALLOWED_CREATION_ROLES`), `transfer-custody` (`:1789`, `ALLOWED_TRANSFER_CUSTODY_ROLES`, declared `:1782`), `version` (`:2263`, `:2258`), `share` (`:2464`, `:2458`), `sign-cert` (`:2936`) and `sign-wallet` (`:3204`) each check a constant built from `DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES` (`middleware/documentWriteRoles.ts:37`: `ISSUER_ADMIN`, `ORG_ADMIN`, `SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN`; the file says at `:24` that `OWNER` is deliberately absent). `revoke` (`:2650`) is owner-only: `if (document.owner?.id !== user.id)` then 403 "Only the owner can revoke this document" (`:2677-2679`). The token census finds no gate in `sign`, `sign/request` or the lifecycle-events routes; I did not read whether they have another kind of check, so this ticket does not claim the retry route is the only route without one. W 7th's comparison, `GET /:id` (`:1078-1217`), is not a role gate either: its matches are the admin cross-tenant fallback terms.

**Layers in front** (read):

* originate `index.ts`: gateway provenance (`:219`), emitter-marker strip (`:223`), the multi-tenancy block (`:226-244`), request tenant resolution (`:259-262`) and `tenantGucContext()` (`:263`). They establish where a request came from and which tenant it is in; none checks a role or an owner.
* `documentsRouter.use(authenticate())` (`documents.ts:175`). `authenticate()` (`middleware/auth.ts:82-137`) verifies the RS256 token and the session; it sets the user and checks no role.
* api-gateway `routes/proxy.ts:657`: `requireScope('documents:read', 'documents:write')` on the whole `/api/documents` mount. `middleware/scopes.ts:34-36` lets JWT and email users straight through ("controlled by RBAC, not scopes"), and `:51` passes an OAuth or API-key caller on ANY ONE of the listed scopes or `*`, with no distinction by method. A search of the gateway's non-test source for `documents:write` and for a method-aware scope check found none for this path. Whether an OAuth or API-key principal reaches originate in a form originate accepts, I did not read (`utils/originateForward.ts`).

**Layer behind** (read): anchoring `index.ts:469` is `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate())`, authentication only. `POST /api/anchors` (`:475`) has no role gate; the only role reference near it is the connector branch (`:554`). [KS-1603](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1603/security-pre-existing-anchoring-post-apianchors-never-checks-who-owns) already tracks that anchoring does not check who owns `documentId`.

**Terminal status** (read): `documentRepo.ts:598` and `:621-622` make the status write `WHEN preserveTerminal AND status IN ('revoked','deleted') THEN status ELSE <new>`, and `preserveTerminalStatuses` defaults to false (documented at `:520-534`, KS-521: the async anchor pipeline "stomped a revoked set by the owner ... so a revoked document verified again"). The create path passes it (`documents.ts:1015`, `:1038`); the retry route does not. `revoke` writes the status only (`documents.ts:2705`), so a revoked document whose blob is absent or `anchor_failed` satisfies the route's entry condition.

**Cost, as logged:** each accepted anchor logs a submission with a fee. Seat D 42nd's demo log shows `"Anchor submitted to Cardano"` with `"fee":179449` (lovelace) in `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatD-42nd/evidence/demo/moved_logs.txt`. Whose wallet pays on each box, I did not verify here.

**Real callers:** Platform S uses this route in its normal flow; KS-1688's comment of 2026-10-19 describes "the anchor kick that follows it (`POST /{newId}/anchor`)" signed with the owning organisation's connector key. Any gate has to keep that principal working; `transfer-custody` shows one shape (a write role OR a scope, documented at `documents.ts:1589-1591`). I am not proposing the fix.

**Not run, not read:** no request to any box; the route was not executed; cross-tenant behaviour beyond the tenant-scoped `getDocument` and the RLS context was not exercised; the gateway's API-key and OAuth path into originate; `sign`, `sign/request` and the lifecycle-events routes, which show no role token.

**Evidence:**

* Source: develop `6d41673e0f79c0f02c2ec7b893cc960b6fa3ec10`, the files named above.
* Seat W 7th's section 16, item 9 (and item 10, the revival): `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatW-7th/KS-1384-per-event-anchor-DESIGN-rev2.md`, lines 496 and 497. Its claim was a lexical count "not verified against upstream middleware"; this ticket is that verification.
* My route census and reads: `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatR-61st/filings/board_search_i.txt` for the board search.

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 17 hits, a random token 0 hits): `documents.ts:1437` 0 hits; "/:id/anchor" 6 hits and "POST /api/documents/:id/anchor" 4 hits, read: [KS-1557](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1557/security-a-write-role-caller-can-make-another-organisations-bytes) (quotes the route name inside an error message), [KS-1385](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1385/ks-1175-follow-on-the-anchors-k-emits-for-share-transfer-custody) (lists the route among six sites that forward identity), [KS-520](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-520/anchoring-fabricates-a-tx-sim-hash-and-marks-the-document-anchored), KS-319, KS-535, KS-566 (archived, other defects); `anchorIdentityFields` 1 hit ([KS-1709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1709/originate-the-certification-issue-route-swallows-a-non-ok-response), other defect); `DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES` 10 hits, read by title: [KS-1688](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1688/security-post-apidocumentsidversion-has-no-per-document-access-check) is the same class on `POST /:id/version` (a missing per-document check on the source document), KS-547 (archived) is a decision about `/certifications/issue`; `preserveTerminalStatuses` 5 hits: KS-1424's table of unguarded `updateDocument` callers lists `documents.ts:1408` and the sync writers, not this route's call at `:1534`. No ticket names this route's missing gate or its missing terminal-status guard.

**Related:** [KS-1688](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1688/security-post-apidocumentsidversion-has-no-per-document-access-check) (same class, the version route), [KS-1603](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1603/security-pre-existing-anchoring-post-apianchors-never-checks-who-owns) (the anchoring side), [KS-485](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-485/security-review-plan-methodology-and-handover-platform-k) (the security review plan).

nodes.title: Refs KS-1814: the anchor retry route checks write role, document access and revoked state

nodes.body:
**The signature path passes too.** Stuart signed the same document at 09:25 UTC, and S routed it as `sign-cert`:
* the version from the watermark version `doc-1793697464044-6730182e` gave `doc-1793697975235-a8273867`;
* `POST /api/documents/doc-1793697975235-a8273867/anchor` gave `anchor_f00b9ab9-7f4a-442a-a445-a86f3eac744f`, with no refusal.

It confirmed at 09:26:46 UTC: tx `c82f24c69bbd5f039e2e4a71ccb9b60ee6513370da7973b7a07c67f1e439a60d`, preview block 4820637. The on-chain `hash` `4815a552…162c` equals S ledger row 116's content hash, which is the signed bytes.

**Platform S's version anchor goes through this route on kintsugi (`b1fb543640e7`), checked live from dev-ps on 3 Nov 2026.** This was the owner case only, not the "live probe" refusal case this ticket still owes.

Stuart watermarked dev-ps document 23 at 09:17 UTC. S's connector key (the owning organisation's) made the usual two calls:
* `POST /api/documents/9d7326ed-476c-47ef-b070-7f7308a78f11/version`, which created `doc-1793697464044-6730182e`.
* `POST /api/documents/doc-1793697464044-6730182e/anchor`, which returned `anchor_97fdb884-d77a-44fe-9d3a-419a7d9a8ec4`. It did not answer 403 or 404: the S log has no refusal.

The anchor **confirmed at 09:20:14 UTC**: tx `7a5e26880011ab6374928ae17c3972b88f34935449e928f0411cfcce11e6e003`, preview block 4820620. Its label 674 metadata, read from Koios:
* `hash` `3343eeef…3f76`, which equals S ledger row 115's content hash (the watermarked bytes, not the upload's `5735d148…`);
* `documentId` and `certId` are both the new version, `doc-1793697464044-6730182e`;
* `type` is `document`.

So the connector key passes `callerMayAnchorDocument` on a version it created. **Not covered here:** the company-admin follow-up, and a refused caller.

**BLUF:** Delivered: PR 1814 merged as 84ddbd63c008 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (2026-11-01; first deployed on 2026-10-30 per the comment on this ticket). Verified by code read, not observed live. Left open: two items from the 2026-10-29 comment are not recorded as done: the live probe of the route (live sweep owed (write)) and the company-admin and transfer-custody follow-up Kam ruled on 2026-10-30.
- **In the code at b1fb543640e7:** `originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1468` (`callerMayAnchorDocument`) and `:1492-1509` put a document-write role or scope check, then per-document access, in front of `POST /api/documents/:id/anchor`; a caller refused on access gets the same 404 an absent document gets.
- **Owed (write):** the live request that exercises the route.
- **Owed, inside this ticket:** until the company-admin follow-up lands, a same-organisation company admin who is not the owner gets 404 (the 2026-10-29 comment).

**Deployed; stays In Progress.** PR #1814 (squash `84ddbd63c00864eba1dc955cc86199fb0c2d17d0`), deployed on develop `e3d8456ec81d` to kintsugi 2026-10-30 09:59:52 AEDT and demo-pk 10:32:01 AEDT. originate was recreated 09:59:15-09:59:28 AEDT (kintsugi) and 10:31:22-10:31:38 AEDT (demo-pk).

- Present in the running originate image on both boxes, by compiled-file fingerprint in `dist/routes/documents.js`: `callerMayAnchorDocument` 3 lines (was 0), the 403 message `Your role / scope does not permit anchoring this document` 1 (was 0), `cannot be anchored` 1 (was 0), `preserveTerminalStatuses: true` 3 (was 2).
- No live request has exercised the route yet. A live probe is owed before Done.
- Still owed on this ticket: the company-admin and transfer-custody follow-up Kam ruled on 2026-10-30 (only if the rights set at the time of creation allow it). Until then a same-organisation company admin who is not the owner gets 404.

**BLUF:** pull request 1814 (head `277e5ba6b7ae8b7f947ef1153ac4c33b4d7c1975`) adds the missing checks to `POST /api/documents/:id/anchor`. It is at READY FOR GATE; it is not merged and not deployed.

* Commit `1f590aa23dff` (Refs KS-1814): every refusal comes before the anchoring call.
  * A document-write role or the `documents:write` scope, else 403, before the document is read.
  * Then a platform admin, the owner or the creating connector, else the same 404 an absent document gets.
  * A revoked or deleted document is refused with 400.
  * The write now passes `preserveTerminalStatuses`.
* Platform S keeps working: its creating connector key re-anchors its own documents, including ownerless ones and `/version`-minted children (cell P1). The S organisation-merge edge is refused, consistent with Kam's card `secuura-ks1688-org-merge-edge-which-side-1020` (a).
* An `OWNER`-role user re-anchors only its own documents. That is the default of card `secuura-ks1814-owner-role-reanchor-1030`, still open.
* Tests:
  * 28 cells, 16 of 28 red against develop's `documents.ts` and 28 of 28 with the change.
  * Seven mutants, each killed alone.
  * The whole originate unit suite passes: 151 files / 1846 cells.
  * Node v26.8.1 (not an LTS line). No stack, no request against any box.
* The four sibling routes are filed, not fixed: KS-1831 (sign), KS-1832 (sign/request), KS-1833 (POST lifecycle-events) and KS-1834 (GET lifecycle-events).

Not done: deploy, the four platform suites, the integration files, and KS-1805 (untouched; next after this merges).
